source_caption:
Catherine O’Hara’s iconic performance as the eccentric, highly dramatic sculptor Delia Deetz almost never happened. The role was originally offered to and accepted by Anjelica Huston, who had to unexpectedly drop out of the production at the last minute due to a sudden illness. O’Hara was quickly brought in as her replacement, a twist of fate that changed her personal life forever. While working on the set, director Tim Burton noticed a genuine spark between O’Hara and the film’s production designer, Bo Welch. Burton strongly encouraged Welch to ask her out, and the two began dating shortly after. They eventually married in 1992, making the haunting of the Deetz family the surprising start to a decades-long Hollywood romance.

Beetlejuice (1988), directed by Tim Burton, starring Michael Keaton, Alec Baldwin, Geena Davis, Winona Ryder, Catherine O’Hara. A recently deceased ghost couple enlists the help of an obnoxious, chaotic “bio-exorcist” to scare away the insufferable new family that has moved into their beloved home.

source_details.synopsis: Beetlejuice is a 1988 American gothic comedy horror film directed by Tim Burton from a screenplay by Michael McDowell and Warren Skaaren based on a story by McDowell and Larry Wilson. The film stars Michael Keaton as Betelgeuse, along with Alec Baldwin, Geena Davis, Jeffrey Jones, Catherine O'Hara, and Winona Ryder. The plot revolves around Adam and Barbara Maitland, a recently deceased couple. As ghosts, they are not allowed to leave their house. They contact Betelgeuse, a sleazy "bio-exorcist", to scare the house's new inhabitants away. The film prominently features music from Harry Belafonte's albums Calypso and Jump Up Calypso. Beetlejuice was released in the United States on March 30, 1
